items.question: What did Chamique Holdsclaw do at Tennessee?
items.answer: Chamique Holdsclaw led Tennessee to three straight NCAA championships, in 1996, 1997 and 1998, and was a two-time Naismith College Player of the Year. She finished as Tennessee's all-time leading scorer and rebounder, men's or women's, with 3,025 points and 1,295 rebounds.

items.question: What did Chamique Holdsclaw average in her WNBA career?
items.answer: Chamique Holdsclaw averaged 16.9 points and 7.6 rebounds per game over her 11-year WNBA career with the Mystics, Sparks, Dream and Silver Stars. In 2002 she became the first WNBA player to lead the league in scoring and rebounding in the same season.

items.question: Is Chamique Holdsclaw in the Hall of Fame?
items.answer: Yes. Chamique Holdsclaw was enshrined in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame on August 15, 2026, in Springfield, Massachusetts. She entered the Women's Basketball Hall of Fame in 2018.

items.question: How old is Chamique Holdsclaw?

items.question: How tall is Chamique Holdsclaw?
items.answer: The WNBA lists Chamique Holdsclaw at 6 feet 2 inches and 172 pounds.

items.question: What is Mind/Game about?
items.answer: Mind/Game: The Unquiet Journey of Chamique Holdsclaw is a documentary directed by Rick Goldsmith. It follows her basketball career and her work as a mental health advocate.

items.question: Who is Chamique Holdsclaw?
items.answer: Chamique Holdsclaw is a Hall of Fame forward from Queens, New York. She won three NCAA titles at Tennessee, went first overall to the Washington Mystics in the 1999 WNBA Draft, won 1999 Rookie of the Year and 2000 Olympic gold, and made six WNBA All-Star teams.

items.question: Was Chamique Holdsclaw on the cover of SLAM?
items.answer: Yes. In 1998, SLAM put Chamique Holdsclaw on the cover of its 29th issue, wearing a full Knicks uniform, before her senior year at Tennessee.

items.question: Where did Chamique Holdsclaw go to high school?
items.answer: Chamique Holdsclaw went to Christ the King High School in Queens, New York, where she won four state championships.
